use_case: Create a highly consistent premium food image for any dish based on a fixed visual style and optional image references.

instructions.core_prompt: Create a photorealistic premium food image of {{DISH_NAME}}. {{OPTIONAL_DISH_DESCRIPTION}} Present the dish in a clean, refined, modern editorial food-photography style matching the reference examples. The food must be shown from a perfect top-down 90-degree overhead view, centered in the frame, on a single perfectly round colored ceramic plate or bowl. CRITICAL: The area outside the plate or bowl must be genuinely transparent alpha, with no backdrop, floor, halo, ambient shadow, drop shadow, texture, or visible surface. The plate itself must be a clean circular cutout. The result must feel like a polished food delivery hero image or premium cookbook product shot.
instructions.style_goal: Keep the visual style extremely consistent across all dishes, regardless of cuisine.
instructions.reinterpretation_rule: If the dish is normally messy, rustic, or informal, reinterpret it into a neat, visually balanced plated presentation while keeping the dish recognizable.
instructions.dish_fidelity_rule: The dish must remain clearly identifiable as {{DISH_NAME}}. Do not transform it into a different recipe.

composition.framing: single dish only, centered, symmetrical or intentionally balanced radial composition
composition.crop: dish fully visible and centred; the circular plate or bowl nearly fills the square canvas without being clipped
composition.background: True transparent alpha outside the plate or bowl. Do not render a tabletop, paper, stone, concrete, marble, linen, vinyl, studio sweep, halo, or shadow. The outer plate edge must be a clean antialiased circular cutout.
composition.scale_consistency: plate or bowl should occupy roughly 70 to 85 percent of the frame
composition.negative_space: transparent alpha only; no visible pixels outside the plate or bowl

plating_rules.structure: main food element must read immediately and clearly
plating_rules.sauce_rule: when suitable, use a smooth puree, sauce bed, or elegant sauce accent to improve composition
plating_rules.garnish_rule: use only small purposeful garnishes such as herbs, microgreens, cracked pepper, parmesan, chili slices, or vegetable accents when appropriate
plating_rules.portioning: avoid overcrowding, keep plating visually organized
plating_rules.geometry: prefer circular, centered, nested, radial, or neatly stacked layouts when suitable
plating_rules.consistency_bias: prioritize visual consistency over chef-level originality

materials_and_props.serveware: single matte or satin-glaze ceramic plate or bowl with subtle handmade texture, same premium ceramic character and finish language as in the reference images
materials_and_props.plate_color_rule: The serveware must always be clearly colored—never plain white, ivory, cream, or undyed porcelain. For each image, choose one random but harmonious ceramic color that contrasts with the food, aligned with the reference style (e.g. deep teal, forest green, sage, terracotta, rust, burnt orange, ochre, slate blue, dusty rose, plum, charcoal glaze, warm brown). Vary the hue across generations while keeping the same material quality and plate vocabulary as the references.
materials_and_props.allowed_props: none except ingredients or garnish that are directly part of the plated dish
forbidden_props: white or cream-colored plates or bowls

lighting_and_rendering.lighting: high-key soft diffused studio lighting on the food and ceramic only — not moody or low-key
lighting_and_rendering.shadow_behavior: No ambient shadow, contact shadow, drop shadow, glow, or halo outside the plate or bowl
lighting_and_rendering.highlights: controlled, no blown highlights on food
lighting_and_rendering.color: natural, appetizing, slightly enhanced but believable
lighting_and_rendering.texture: high detail on food and ceramic only; everything outside the plate is transparent
lighting_and_rendering.focus: entire dish sharp and in focus
lighting_and_rendering.render_style: photorealistic premium food photography with a clean transparent cutout

must_be: genuine transparent alpha outside the circular plate or bowl
must_not_be: white, gray, coloured, or textured backdrop
background noise, halo, shadow, glow, gradient, or vignette
white, cream, or ivory plate or bowl
marble, concrete, tile, or wood visible as surface

reference_strategy.reference_use_instruction: Use the reference images for style consistency: composition, lighting on the food, presentation language, and especially the type of colored matte ceramics and surface quality. For the BACKDROP ONLY: ignore every backdrop or shadow present in references and output genuine transparent alpha. Do not copy the exact food from the references unless it matches {{DISH_NAME}}. Pick a plate color that could belong in the same set as the references but may differ hue per image.

fallback_behavior.for_soups: Use a centered round bowl, smooth surface, elegant cream swirl or oil ring, minimal garnish in the center. Transparent outside the bowl.
fallback_behavior.for_pasta: Keep pasta neatly twirled or clearly arranged on a round coloured plate; avoid chaotic scattered noodles. Transparent outside the plate.
fallback_behavior.for_pizza: Use one complete centered circular pizza in overhead view, with transparent alpha outside its edge.
fallback_behavior.for_wraps_or_tacos: Use a clean open presentation viewed top-down on a round coloured plate, with organized fillings and restrained garnish. Transparent outside the plate.
fallback_behavior.for_curries_or_stews: Use a refined round bowl or plate presentation with clearly separated rice or accompaniment if appropriate. Transparent outside the serveware.
fallback_behavior.for_rustic_dishes: Clean up the composition and simplify the plating without losing recognizability. Use a round coloured plate and transparent alpha outside it.

final_generation_prompt: CRITICAL TRANSPARENCY — READ FIRST: Every pixel outside the perfectly round coloured ceramic plate or bowl must be genuine transparent alpha. Render no backdrop, tabletop, studio sweep, halo, ambient shadow, contact shadow, drop shadow, glow, texture, paper grain, concrete, marble, gradient, or vignette. The circular serveware edge must be clean and antialiased. Create a photorealistic premium studio food image of {{DISH_NAME}}. {{OPTIONAL_DISH_DESCRIPTION}} Match the reference images for: overhead 90-degree top-down view, one centered circular coloured ceramic plate or bowl that nearly fills the square canvas (never white or cream ceramic; choose a random contrasting matte glaze in the same family as references: teal, green, terracotta, rust, slate blue, dusty rose, charcoal glaze, etc.), soft diffused food lighting on the subject only, elegant premium plating, realistic textures on food and ceramic, balanced composition, subtle purposeful garnish, no props, cutlery, hands, clutter, or text. The dish must stay clearly recognizable as {{DISH_NAME}}; reinterpret into a clean refined presentation if needed. Ignore any backdrop or shadow present in the reference images.
